title: Binary Search: Interval Conventions, Boundary Updates, and Applicability
evidence_note: The supplied fixture chunk (fixture_binary_search_en) directly supports one easy MCQ on the closed-interval midpoint update rule for an ascending distinct-value array; no additional material is needed.
learning_objectives: Recall the closed-interval [left, right] convention and its boundary update rules for binary search.
Identify the correct midpoint update when the middle value is smaller than the target.

questions.stem: Using the closed interval [left, right] convention for binary search on an ascending array with distinct values, suppose the middle value is smaller than the target. Which boundary update is correct?
questions.explanation: In the closed-interval convention, if the middle value is smaller than the target, every position through mid is too small, so the eligible interval becomes [mid + 1, right].
questions.difficulty_reason: This is a direct recall of one explicit boundary update rule from the notes; it requires only remembering and understanding the stated closed-interval convention.

concepts: boundary update when middle value is smaller than target
expected_steps: Recall that the closed interval [left, right] includes both endpoints.
When the middle value is smaller than the target, discard mid and all positions to its left by setting left = mid + 1.

visual_prompt: A horizontal array of sorted ascending numbers with a closed interval bracket [left, right] underneath. A midpoint marker sits at index mid. An arrow shows the middle value being smaller than the target, and the left bracket moves to mid + 1 while the right bracket stays at right.
